youtube.title: Is the Caspian Sea a Lake? Bigger Than Germany, Not Legally a Sea
youtube.description:
Is the Caspian Sea a lake or a sea? For five countries, the answer decides who owns roughly 48 billion barrels of oil and a vast store of gas. We follow the map from the 1813 Treaty of Gulistan to the 2018 Aktau convention, which calls the Caspian neither, and look at the dispute between Iran and its neighbours over the Caspian oil and gas under the seabed.

We follow the map from the 1813 Treaty of Gulistan to the 2018 Aktau convention, which calls the Caspian neither. We cover the lines drawn in the north, the empty south, Iran's case and its neighbours' case, and three things that could redraw the map, including a shrinking shoreline.

{CHAPTERS}

youtube.comment: Sea, lake, or neither: what would you call the Caspian? 👇

sources.claim: The Caspian is about 1,200 km long
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Caspian Sea'

sources.claim: The Caspian basin holds an estimated 48 billion barrels of oil
sources.source: US Energy Information Administration, Caspian Sea Region overview, August 2013 (proved and probable, onshore and offshore)

sources.claim: 292 trillion cubic feet of gas around the basin
sources.source: US EIA, Caspian Sea Region overview, August 2013

sources.claim: Under a median line Iran would get about 13 percent; estimates range from 11 to 14 percent
sources.source: Reuters and Al Jazeera coverage of the Aktau summit, 12 August 2018; B. Mehdiyoun, American Journal of International Law, vol. 94, 2000

sources.claim: Iran has argued for 20 percent, an equal share for each coastal state
sources.source: Reuters, 12 August 2018; Mehdiyoun, AJIL 2000

sources.claim: Caspian oil leaves by pipeline to Mediterranean and Black Sea ports
sources.source: BP Azerbaijan, Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline; Caspian Pipeline Consortium (to Novorossiysk)

sources.claim: Largest inland body of water on Earth, about 371,000 square kilometres
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Caspian Sea'

sources.claim: Germany covers 357,588 square kilometres
sources.source: Destatis, Federal Statistical Office of Germany

sources.claim: The south drops to about 1,025 metres
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Caspian Sea'

sources.claim: The Eiffel Tower is 330 metres tall
sources.source: Société d'Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel, official site

sources.claim: The north averages about five metres deep and freezes in winter
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Caspian Sea'

sources.claim: The Volga brings in about four fifths of the Caspian's inflow; no outflow to the ocean
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Caspian Sea'

sources.claim: The surface lies about 28 metres below sea level
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Caspian Sea' (level varies year to year)

sources.claim: Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli is Azerbaijan's biggest oil field, more than 100 km off Baku
sources.source: BP Azerbaijan, ACG field page

sources.claim: Kashagan was found in 2000, south-east of Atyrau
sources.source: North Caspian Operating Company (NCOC), Kashagan project page

sources.claim: Treaty of Gulistan signed October 1813; Persia ceded Caucasus khanates including Baku
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Treaty of Gulistan'

sources.claim: Gulistan gave Russia alone the right to warships on the Caspian
sources.source: Treaty of Gulistan, Article V, in J.C. Hurewitz, The Middle East and North Africa in World Politics, 1975

sources.claim: Treaty of Turkmenchay, 1828, fixed the border at the Astara river
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Treaty of Turkmenchay'

sources.claim: By 1900 Baku produced about half of the world's oil
sources.source: Daniel Yergin, The Prize, 1991; Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Baku'

sources.claim: 1921 treaty gave both equal navigation rights
sources.source: Treaty of Friendship between Persia and the RSFSR, 26 February 1921, League of Nations Treaty Series vol. 9

sources.claim: 1940 treaty called the Caspian 'a Soviet and Iranian sea'
sources.source: Soviet-Iranian Treaty of Commerce and Navigation, 25 March 1940, exchange of letters; cited in Mehdiyoun, AJIL 2000

sources.claim: Ten-nautical-mile fishing zones under the 1940 treaty
sources.source: Soviet-Iranian Treaty of Commerce and Navigation, 25 March 1940, Article 12

sources.claim: In 1970 the Soviet oil ministry divided its seabed into sectors for four republics
sources.source: Mehdiyoun, AJIL 2000; Zimnitskaya & von Geldern, Journal of International Affairs, 2011

sources.claim: The Astara-Hasankuli line, which Iran says it never accepted
sources.source: Mehdiyoun, AJIL 2000; Zimnitskaya & von Geldern, 2011

sources.claim: The Soviet Union dissolved in December 1991
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Soviet Union'

sources.claim: Contract of the Century signed 20 September 1994
sources.source: BP Azerbaijan, ACG production sharing agreement history

sources.claim: Russia protested that unilateral development was unlawful
sources.source: Letter from the Russian Federation to the UN Secretary-General, UN doc A/49/475, 5 October 1994

sources.claim: Russia and Kazakhstan split the northern seabed by a modified median line in 1998
sources.source: Russia-Kazakhstan agreement of 6 July 1998; US EIA Caspian overview, 2013

sources.claim: Kazakhstan-Azerbaijan 2001, Russia-Azerbaijan 2002, trilateral 2003
sources.source: US EIA, Caspian Sea Region overview, August 2013

sources.claim: On 23 July 2001 an Iranian warship ordered a BP survey ship out of the Alov field; BP stopped work
sources.source: BBC News, 24 July 2001; The New York Times, 25 July 2001

sources.claim: Iran calls the field Alborz
sources.source: BBC News, 24 July 2001

sources.claim: Median lines divide the North Sea's oil
sources.source: UK-Norway Continental Shelf Agreement, 10 March 1965

sources.claim: Five presidents signed the convention in Aktau on 12 August 2018 after more than two decades of talks
sources.source: Kremlin.ru, 12 August 2018; talks began in a working group in 1996 (Reuters, 12 August 2018)

sources.claim: The convention calls the Caspian a body of water surrounded by the land territories of the Parties
sources.source: Convention on the Legal Status of the Caspian Sea, 12 August 2018, Article 1

sources.claim: 15-nautical-mile territorial waters and a 10-mile fishing zone
sources.source: Convention on the Legal Status of the Caspian Sea, 2018, Articles 7 and 9

sources.claim: The seabed is divided by agreements between neighbouring states
sources.source: Convention on the Legal Status of the Caspian Sea, 2018, Article 8

sources.claim: No armed forces from outside the five
sources.source: Convention on the Legal Status of the Caspian Sea, 2018, Article 3

sources.claim: On 7 October 2015 the Caspian Flotilla fired 26 cruise missiles at targets in Syria
sources.source: Russian Ministry of Defence, reported by Reuters, 7 October 2015

sources.claim: Iran's parliament has not ratified; the convention takes force only after all five ratify
sources.source: Convention, final provisions; Tehran Times and Reuters reporting through 2024

sources.claim: In January 2021 Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan agreed to develop the Kapaz/Serdar field, renamed Dostluk
sources.source: Reuters, 21 January 2021; Office of the President of Azerbaijan

sources.claim: Trans-Caspian gas pipeline of about 300 km from Turkmenbashi to Baku
sources.source: European Commission, Southern Gas Corridor documents; Reuters, 2021

sources.claim: A pipeline route needs agreement only with the states whose seabed sectors it crosses, plus environmental standards
sources.source: Convention on the Legal Status of the Caspian Sea, 2018, Article 14

sources.claim: Russia and Iran have raised environmental objections; Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan say the project can meet the rules
sources.source: Reuters reporting, 2018-2021

sources.claim: Iran said in 2018 that seabed limits still need a separate agreement
sources.source: President Hassan Rouhani at the Aktau summit, reported by Reuters, 12 August 2018

sources.claim: A 2020 study projected a fall of 9 to 18 metres by 2100, mainly from warming-driven evaporation; about a quarter of the surface lost at 9 metres
sources.source: Prange, Wilke & Wesselingh, Communications Earth & Environment, December 2020

sources.claim: Kazakhstan reports the water dropping along its coast
sources.source: Kazakhstan Ministry of Ecology statements, 2023; Reuters, 2023

sources.claim: Turkmen gas flows mostly east to China
sources.source: Energy Institute, Statistical Review of World Energy, 2024

sources.claim: The Trans-Caspian pipeline plan dates from the late 1990s
sources.source: Reuters; US EIA Caspian overview, 2013

sources.claim: The Volga-Don Canal links the Caspian basin to the Black Sea
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Volga-Don Canal' (opened 1952)

sources.claim: The Wakhan Corridor was drawn as a buffer between the British and Russian empires
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Wakhan Corridor'
